inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E: 9M FY2026 net sales 18,172 (Q3-2026 10-Q) + Q4 ~6,030 (Q4-2025 6,006 actual; Q3-2026 run-rate 6,197 less seasonality). Continuing operations only -- Global Cellulose Fibers sold 2026-01-23 and excluded throughout.
inputs.share_count_basis: 627.0M issued less 97.5M treasury = 529.5M outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet), plus ~2.5M unvested RSU/PSU dilution (Q3 diluted count 529.6M excludes them only because the quarter was loss-making). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. No open-market buybacks since 2023 ($2.96bn authorisation unused), so the flat count is a modelling convention IP is not currently funding. The 2025 DS Smith share issuance (~180M shares) is already in the base count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Notes payable/current maturities 2,203 + long-term debt 7,488 (includes finance leases 97) less cash and temporary investments 815, all at 2026-09-30. Operating lease liabilities (~$0.6bn) EXCLUDED: under US GAAP operating lease cost already sits inside cost of products sold and therefore inside adjusted EBITDA (lease treatment B). VIE timber-note financial assets 2,363 and non-recourse VIE liabilities 2,132 are excluded on both sides (the 231 net is offset by deferred tax on the original forestland gains). Net pension/OPEB surplus (+564 overfunded, -294 underfunded, -126 postretirement = +144 pre-tax) excluded as immaterial.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not deducted: IP is net-debt (8.9bn). The ~$180M/yr 'interest income' line is mostly VIE timber-note income that offsets VIE non-recourse interest; neither side is in the unlevered flows or the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: Q3-2026 10-Q stock-based compensation note: $78M for 9M FY2026 (annualised ~$104M); restricted-stock tax withholding $31M for 9M FY2026 (annualised ~$40M) from the financing section. No combined figure is published, so the two lines are summed. FY2025 10-K: SBC $93M + withholding $65M; FY2024 $77M + $23M. IP's Adjusted EBITDA does NOT add back SBC, so ebitda_margin_path is Adjusted EBITDA + SBC (pre-SBC) and SBC is charged separately via sbc_pct_path.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular-session close (Friday); Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~9.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (BBB) -> ~4.2% after tax; market weights ~67% equity / 33% net debt -> ~7.7%, rounded up to 8.0%. Same WACC in all scenarios: cyclicality, EMEA execution and dividend-coverage risk are charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in the discount rate.
inputs.terminal_rationale: Terminal growth 2.0% (mature containerboard: ~flat volume, inflation pricing). Cap multiple 15x terminal unlevered owner FCF -- top of the 12-15x cyclical band because IP's FCF conversion is structurally low (capex ~= D&A ~40% of EBITDA): 15x FCF is only ~6.3x base terminal EBITDA, at or below the 7-8x EV/EBITDA containerboard has traded at through the cycle. Gordon at 8%/2% (~17x) exceeds the cap in all scenarios, so the cap binds.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating cost): US GAAP operating lease expense is already inside cost of products sold, hence inside adjusted EBITDA; lease_cost_pct_path = 0 and operating lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. Finance leases (97) are in total_debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests; consolidated flows equal attributable flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, US filer, cyclical). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (leases, charge-risk-once). First valuation of IP -- no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF. FY0 is FY2026E (nine months actual + Q4 implied by guidance) because FY2025 carried 11 months of DS Smith, the GCF business (sold Jan-2026) and $700M+ of accelerated depreciation; it is not a usable base. Year 1 = FY2027. GCF is excluded from all forward flows; its $1.1bn cash proceeds are already in the 2026-09-30 cash/debt, and the $168M AIP preferred stock received is added in the equity bridge. EMEA SEPARATION: management's planned taxable spin-off 'or another strategic alternative' (Q3-2026 10-Q) is NOT baked in -- a spin distributes EMEA to the same shareholders and is value-neutral in a whole-company DCF; separation costs and dis-synergies are absorbed in the margin paths; a sale above the DCF value of EMEA is a bull catalyst, not a modelled proceeds line. FY2026 FCF guidance cut to ~$100-200M (reported_fcf uses the $150M midpoint; this is levered and after ~$0.4bn of interest and restructuring/separation cash) against a ~$975M dividend: the dividend is not covered by FCF and is debt-funded in 2026. That matters for the balance sheet path and is reflected in the bear weight, but dividends are a distribution, not a cost, in the DCF. GOVERNANCE: disclosure controls not effective at 2026-09-30 (legacy DS Smith ITGC material weakness, remediation expected only after separation) -- a risk note, not a valuation driver. Recurring 'special items' (restructuring, closure costs) run at hundreds of millions every year at IP; the mature EBITDA margins below are set ~0.3-0.5pp under what an unadjusted 'adjusted EBITDA' trajectory would imply to charge for them.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: organic price + volume for mature containerboard; every historical CAGR is distorted by the DS Smith all-stock acquisition (Jan-2025) and the GCF/printing-papers exits
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (20.4% 3yr, 13.5% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (3.8%/6.1%) because ~180M shares were issued for DS Smith -- book growth is acquisition accounting, not compounding; since then $3.8bn of EMEA goodwill has been impaired. EPS CAGRs undefined (FY2025 EPS -6.95). Not used.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs on the Metrics CSV basis: FY2022 21,161 includes GCF (3,227); on a restated ex-GCF basis (17,934) the 3yr CAGR is 9.6%, all of it the DS Smith acquisition. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - restricted-stock withholding (no interest-income deduction; net debt): FY2023 692-53-21=618, FY2024 757-77-23=657, FY2025 -159-93-65=-317, FY2026E 150-104-40=6 (guidance midpoint). Owner-FCF CAGRs undefined (sign change). SBC is small (~0.6% of revenue), so the SBC adjustment is not the story here; the collapse is capex up (921 -> ~2,050), interest up and EMEA losses.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +3%: NORPAC (acquired Jun-2026) full-year effect ~+1% and 2026 price increases carrying over, against soft volumes. Then 2.5-3% (price ~2%, volume ~0.5-1%) fading to 2% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026E pre-SBC EBITDA ~12.8% (9M adj EBITDA 2,107 + Q4 ~890 + SBC ~104, on 24,200). PS NA guided to $1.3-1.4bn OP in FY2026 with Q4 at $460-500M (a ~$1.9bn annualised run-rate); base takes PS NA to ~19-20% EBITDA and PS EMEA to ~9-10% (low-single-digit OP margin) by FY2030 -> blended ~16.5% after corporate cost and recurring special items. Well short of the 20% management implied when DS Smith was bought; at the level Smurfit WestRock earns.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A ~8.4% of FY2026E sales (9M 1,503) includes DS Smith intangible amortisation; it fades as the intangibles amortise and the impaired EMEA asset base shrinks. Capex guided $2.0-2.1bn in FY2026 (~8.5%, Riverdale conversion, greenfield box plants, catch-up maintenance) normalising to IP's historical ~6-6.5% of sales by FY2032; terminal capex = D&A.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: receivables 4,324 + contract assets 640 + inventory 2,119 - payables 4,149 = ~2,934, ~12% of sales. Growth consumes cash, so capture is negative.
base.tax_rationale: US federal 21% + state + EMEA mix ~24% normal cash rate; FY2027-28 slightly lower on GCF capital losses and 2026 audit settlements. Tax is charged on positive EBIT only.

scenario_narratives.base: PS NA keeps compounding the 2026 recovery: price increases stick, Riverdale and NORPAC lower the mill cost curve, 80/20 cost-out continues, and segment EBITDA margins reach ~19-20% by FY2030 -- roughly where Q4-2026 guidance annualises. PS EMEA stops losing money but does not become a good business: soft European box demand, energy costs and the larger Smurfit WestRock competitor hold it to a low-single-digit operating margin. Whether EMEA is spun, sold or kept, its cash flows are counted once in the whole. Capex falls from the ~$2bn 2026 peak back toward historical ~6.5% of sales, which is what turns a ~$0 owner FCF year into ~$2bn by the end of the decade. The dividend stays debt-funded through 2027 and is covered from 2028.
scenario_narratives.bull: North American containerboard tightens (capacity closures, including IP's own, plus fiber substitution for plastic) and IP gets to PKG-like ~22% PS NA EBITDA margins; the EMEA separation either crystallises a sale at a price that stops the bleeding or the standalone company executes a turnaround to ~12% EBITDA. Synergy run-rate keeps growing past the $710M achieved by end-FY2025, revenue grows 3-4.5% early on price and bolt-ons, and capex normalises faster because the Riverdale/greenfield programme is complete. Blended EBITDA ~19%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The DS Smith deal stays a value destroyer: PS EMEA remains loss-making through the cycle (more impairments after the $3.8bn already taken), separation is delayed or done at a forced-seller price with dis-synergies and stranded costs, and the 2025-26 soft demand persists in both regions. PS NA margins stall in the mid-teens as input costs (energy, recovered fiber, diesel) outrun price. Capex cannot be cut much below 7% without starving the mills. Blended EBITDA plateaus ~13.5%, owner FCF stays under $1.3bn, and with $8.9bn of net debt the equity absorbs nearly all of the shortfall -- the dividend (~$1bn) would have to be cut.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: FCF has been negative or near-zero two years running against a ~$1bn dividend, EMEA has absorbed $3.8bn of impairments and loses money every quarter, net debt is ~4x FY2026E EBITDA after the DS Smith deal, and the separation path is now explicitly uncertain. Base 50%: Q3-2026 PS NA inflection and Q4 guidance are real evidence the North American recovery is underway. Bull cut to 25% from 35% because it needs two independent things -- a North American pricing cycle AND an EMEA turnaround or good-price exit -- to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: IP is a levered, cyclical, low-FCF-conversion containerboard producer two years into digesting an acquisition that has so far destroyed value. With ~$8.9bn of net debt against ~$18bn of market cap, small changes in mid-cycle EBITDA margin move the equity a lot. The valuation hinges on one number -- where blended EBITDA margin settles once capex normalises -- and the current price already requires the base case's ~16.5% to be achieved.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is roughly $0.3bn of owner FCF and ~$8-9/share at a 15x terminal multiple
Capex normalisation: if IP needs ~7.5% of sales in perpetuity rather than ~6.5%, terminal FCF falls ~$0.3bn
PS EMEA: further impairments, separation dis-synergies, or a forced sale below value; IP has stopped guiding the segment
Leverage and dividend: FY2026 FCF guide (~$100-200M) does not cover a ~$975M dividend; continued debt funding raises net debt and credit-rating risk
Governance: disclosure controls not effective (legacy DS Smith ITGC material weakness) until after separation -- raises the chance of restatement or late surprises, not a direct value driver
Terminal cap multiple: the cap binds in all scenarios; at a 13x cap every scenario falls ~$4-6/share
